verdicts.title: Formal Barycenter Spaces with Weights: The Euler Characteristic
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We compute the Euler characteristic with compact supports $χ_c$ of the formal barycenter spaces with weights of a finite CW complex, connected or not. This reduces to the topological Euler characteristic $χ$ when the weights of the singular points are less than one. As foresighted by A. Malchiodi, our formula is related to the Leray-Schauder degree for mean field equations on a compact Riemann surface obtained by C.C. Chen and C.S. Lin.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns Euler characteristics of formal barycenter spaces with weights connected to mean field equations on Riemann surfaces, with no mention of directed flag complexes, SAT formulas, or DPLL backtracking — it shares only the vocabulary 'Euler characteristic'.

verdicts.title: Finiteness obstructions and Euler characteristics of categories
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We introduce notions of finiteness obstruction, Euler characteristic, L^2-Euler characteristic, and Möbius inversion for wide classes of categories. The finiteness obstruction of a category Gamma of type (FP) is a class in the projective class group K_0(RGamma); the functorial Euler characteristic and functorial L^2-Euler characteristic are respectively its RGamma-rank and L^2-rank. We also extend the second author's K-theoretic Möbius inversion from finite categories to quasi-finite categories.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns Euler characteristics and Möbius inversion for categories (proper orbit category, groupoid cardinality), with no mention of directed flag complexes, SAT formulas, or DPLL search — it shares only the general vocabulary of 'Euler characteristic.'

verdicts.title: The topology of critical processes, III (Computing homotopy)
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
Directed Algebraic Topology studies spaces equipped with a form of direction, to include models of non-reversible processes. In the present extension we also want to cover critical processes, indecomposable and unstoppable.
  The previous parts of this series introduced controlled spaces and their fundamental category. Here we study how to compute the latter. The homotopy structure of these spaces will be examined in Part IV.

verdicts.title: Directed Homology and Persistence Modules
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this note, we give a self-contained account on a construction for a directed homology theory based on modules over algebras, linking it to both persistence homology and natural homology. We study its first properties, among which some exact sequences.
